chapter_theme: Three songs at Avinasi (அவிநாசி) in Kongu: a plea to the guru to end death and birth, courtesans who take coins, and old age with the coming of Death's messengers; Murugan is also praised in the person of Sambandar.

943.reading: A short song: the poet asks Murugan to become his true guru and rule him so that he neither dies nor is born again, and to give him the steadfast great life. The praise calls him the Kura girl's husband, Guha, Kumaresa of the Word, the one who declares the four, at Avinasi.
943.nuance: இறவாமல் பிறவாமல்: release is named as the end of both death and birth. அறநாலைப் புகல்வோனே may mean he who speaks the four Vedas or the four aims of life; the text does not say which.

944.reading: The poet describes courtesans of the street who take coins as their share, rosewater-scented, flower-crowned, lotus-mouthed, who greet with folded hands and are idle, and says that even if he sinks in love into their beds he will not forget the lotus feet that the gods bow to. The praise seems to identify Murugan with Sambandar, who made a girl from bones and sang Tamil at the Sangam so that the Jains were impaled, and names the vel that burned the demons and restored Indra to Amaravati, at Avinasi in Kongu.
944.nuance: பங்குக் கைக் காசுகொள் வேசியர்: the coin taken as their share marks these as courtesans. As in 936, the plea is a vow not to forget the feet even in their beds. அங்கத்தைப் பாவை செய்தாம் ... கழு ஏறிட points to Sambandar's raising of Poompavai from her bones and to the impaling of the Jains at Madurai; the opening lines of the praise are obscure.

945.reading: The poet pictures old age, phlegm rising, black hair grey, eyes dimmed, gait faltering, mother, wife and children disgusted and kin mocking with abuse, and asks that before Death's messengers come in anger with noose and trident to drag him away, Murugan come on the peacock and give his paired feet; he asks also to think of him daily in rich Tamil and that Murugan dwell in his mind as his life's companion. The praise names the vel that split Sura in the sea into the cock and the peacock, Kumaresa who told the hidden meaning to Hara, whose feet Brahma and Vishnu searched for, and Avinasi, where Brahmins who give dharma worship daily.
945.nuance: The plea moves from the body's decay to the household's contempt (வசைக்குறும் சொலினால் மிகவே தினம் நகையாட) to the messengers, then asks for the feet before they seize him (பிடிக்கு முன்). அரற்கு அரும்பொருள் தான் உரை கூறிய is the teaching of Siva without naming Om.

links.note: Both meet Death's messengers by turning to the Lord in time: the Tirumanthiram says that for one who thinks of the Lord the messengers will not even think of burning him, and 945 asks for the feet before the messengers with noose and trident seize him.

Both draw old age in the same order, grey hair, failing eyes and teeth, phlegm and cough, then the family's contempt: in 945 kin mock, in 955 the wife reviles and all call him unclean, and both ask for grace at the hour that follows.

The song asks Murugan to become the true guru so that the poet neither dies nor is born (இறவாமல் பிறவாமல்). Tirumanthiram 2585 says the Lord he never forgot set him here so that he would not die and be born again (இறந்து பிறவாமல் ஈங்கு வைத்தானே). What the hymn asks for, the Tirumanthiram reports as granted, in nearly the same words.

source_issues: Song 945: நீனைத்தினம் (line 23) is probably a misspelling of நினைத்தினம்.
